newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM, Nedlloyd say no comment on Martinair link.
newsitem.headline: KLM, Nedlloyd say no comment on Martinair link.

text.p: Dutch carrier KLM on Wednesday declined to comment on reports it was re-assessing its relationship with Martinair, a 50-50 freight and passenger joint venture with Rotterdam-based transport firm Nedlloyd.

Dutch newspaper NRC Handelsblad reported that KLM was mulling either the sale of its 50 percent stake or the acquisition of the remainder from Nedlloyd, which has long ceased to regard Martinair as a core activity.
"We have no comment to make on the NRC story or similar reports," KLM spokeswoman Marjolein Wenting said.

Nedlloyd spokesman Herman Lammerst van Buren also declined to comment on the article beyond saying no agreement existed with KLM on the sale of Nedlloyd's 50 percent stake to the Dutch carrier after Martinair director Martin Schroeder retired next year.
"No agreements such as those alleged in the (NRC) article exist between Nedlloyd and KLM," Lammerst van Buren said.
